clue.text: Nan and niece leaving church splitting bishop's liqueur

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother, a grandma

indicators.note: splitting says the bishop's letters are forced apart by what goes between them

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation used for a bishop

indicators.note: leaving says the church letters walk out of the word niece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Grandmother and niece walk out of church and break into the bishop's bottle of liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nan' looks like a person in the scene but stands for GRANDMA; RR is the Right Reverend, a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Marnier is a French orange-flavoured brandy-based liqueur, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Chase farm animal biting fine queen

indicators.note: biting says the goat's mouth closes round the next piece

parts.note: a goat is a farm animal
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a queen

explanation.surface: A farmyard goat nips a queen and gets chased.
explanation.definitionFit: To go after someone is to pursue them, a phrase meaning to chase.

clue.text: Symbolic system a garble when misrepresented

indicators.note: misrepresented means given a false shape, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A code of symbols turns into gibberish when misrepresented.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of maths that uses letters and symbols to stand for numbers, a symbolic system.

clue.text: Pretend dive heartless, involving Argentine player overturned on ball oddly

indicators.note: involving says the outer letters wrap round what follows
heartless removes the middle of the word dive, keeping its ends
overturned says the player's name is turned upside down, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Lionel Messi is an Argentine footballer

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of ball

explanation.surface: A footballer's dive, with Messi tumbling over the ball, is a feint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless', 'overturned' and 'oddly' each work on one word; 'involving' then wraps the ends of dive round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to conceal one's real motives, a synonym of pretend.

clue.text: Getting on part of crag in gorge

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mountaineer getting on, partway up a crag in a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'Getting' as the definition, leaving 'on' unexplained; the definition is the phrase 'Getting on', meaning growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, which is what ageing means.

clue.text: Spill the beans about alien's short message

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to let on is to reveal a secret, to spill the beans
ET, the extraterrestrial, is a film alien

explanation.surface: Someone reveals the secret of an alien's brief note.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for writing a brief note on.

clue.text: Mimic native Australian beast and others climbing

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird found only in Australia

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: An Australian creature and its companions copy one another up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to imitate them in hope of matching them, a synonym of mimic.

clue.text: Cereal is first of products in fast food item

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the word for fast

parts.note: hasty means quick, fast

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word products

explanation.surface: Cereal tops a list of fast-food products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' reads as one phrase, but 'fast' is HASTY and 'food item' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish pasty is a baked pastry filled with meat and vegetables, a traditional dish from Cornwall in England.

clue.text: Fruit an ogre's pulped

indicators.note: pulped means crushed to a mush, so the letters of these words are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An ogre has crushed some fruit to pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits, so the answer is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Really current books and old book

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Something genuinely topical about books, both new and old.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In truth' is an adverbial phrase meaning actually or honestly, a synonym of really.

clue.text: Moving to coach with hotel drink

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Transferring to a coach with a hotel on the itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate is a warm cocoa beverage, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Famous aristo hiding at back

indicators.note: hiding says the noble wraps round and conceals the other piece

parts.note: an aristocrat is a noble

indicators.note: back says the word at is read backwards

explanation.surface: A well-known aristocrat skulks out of sight at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the word 'at', and 'hiding' tucks it inside the aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is worthy of notice and widely known, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: Good six-footer comprising everything heroic

indicators.note: comprising says the first pieces hold the second within them

parts.note: an ant is an insect, and insects have six legs or feet
everything means all

explanation.surface: A worthy six-footer contains everything that makes a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant describes brave, chivalrous conduct, a synonym of heroic.

clue.text: Revolutionary songs about unknown land

indicators.note: about says the reversed songs go round the unknown
revolutionary means turning round, so the songs are read backwards

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
Y is one of the letters used for an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Rebel songs about some unidentified country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns AIRS into SRIA, and 'about' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in the Middle East, an example of a land.

clue.text: Aboard vessel, note husband's prominent facial features

indicators.note: aboard says the note is placed on board, inside, the vessel

parts.note: a bucket is a vessel for carrying liquid
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: On a ship, someone notices a husband's striking face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aboard' looks nautical, but the 'vessel' is a pail, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck teeth are upper front teeth that jut forward, so they are noticeable features of the face.

clue.text: Fellow player mostly sour, from south country

parts.note: a co-star is a fellow actor in a production

indicators.note: from south in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
mostly says the last letter of the word for sour is dropped

parts.note: acid means sour

explanation.surface: A sulky fellow player from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ACID to ACI, which 'from south' turns into ICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a nation in Central America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Female supporter at person's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of these words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman backing a cause appears at somebody's broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A patroness is a woman who sponsors or backs an artist or cause, a female patron.

clue.text: Preview something that's drawn

definitions.meaning: a short advance showing of a film

explanation.surface: A sneak peek at something sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests a picture, but it means towed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is both a promotional film clip and a wheeled unit hauled by a car or lorry.

clue.text: Supervised deliveries put on cutter

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Deliveries are put onto a cutting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, so its past tense oversaw means supervised.

clue.text: Important horse not well, we're told

indicators.note: we're told says the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse; not well means sick

explanation.surface: A significant horse is reported to be unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental or essential, so in the sense of being central it is near to important.

clue.text: Not completely set in ground, trim plant

indicators.note: not completely says the last letter of the word for set in ground is lost

parts.note: to bury is to set something in the ground
to dock is to cut short, trim

explanation.surface: Not fully planted out, a tidy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdock is a coarse weed with hooked burrs, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Rescuer of various bats

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters of the word are put into a mad new order

explanation.surface: Someone saves a variety of bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals being rescued, but as an adjective meaning crazy it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A saviour is someone who saves another from danger, a synonym of rescuer.

clue.text: Moment over for reorganisation

parts.note: a shake is a moment, as in 'in two shakes'
up means over or finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: The moment has passed, time for a reorganisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a radical overhaul of an organisation or system.

clue.text: Face: I see pronounced terror

parts.note: pan is slang for the face

indicators.note: pronounced says the words are taken as spoken aloud

parts.note: the words I see, spoken, sound like two letters

explanation.surface: A face: 'I see,' it says in horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a synonym of terror.

clue.text: A round's beginning with opponent's entry

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word round's

parts.note: a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: A boxing round opens with an opponent stepping into the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is a coming in, so it shares the sense of an entrance or entry.

clue.text: Former leader and the old soldier fall from grace

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
Lt, lieutenant, is an army officer, so a soldier
to sin is to fall from grace, and a sin is such a fall

explanation.surface: An ex-leader and a veteran soldier both disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of Russia after the Soviet Union, a past head of state.

clue.text: Settle one negative in defeat

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in says the negative is placed inside the defeat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Someone resolves a loss by a single no vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out a problem is to resolve it, an idiom that means to settle it.

clue.text: Asian snack reflected new twist — great thing!

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to warp is to twist out of shape
a cracker is informally something excellent

explanation.surface: A mirror shows a fresh twist on a real winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns N and WARP into PRAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawn crackers are puffed crisps served with Chinese and South-East Asian food, a kind of snack.
